key_insight: CARM masks entire LLM responses by averaging the absolute token log-ratios, so opposite policy shifts cannot cancel and hide off-policy drift.
engineering_relevance: This gives RL practitioners a more reliable sequence-level filter for post-training updates when rollout and training engines differ, helping stabilize mathematical reasoning and code-generation optimization.
method: Compute per-token log probability ratios between sampled and training policies.
Take absolute values before length-normalized averaging to prevent cancellation.
Accept only responses that satisfy the proposed band-based drift bounds.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, CARM improves mean@16 on AIME 2024/2025/2026 and BeyondAIME by up to 3.13 points, and boosts average pass@1 on four code benchmarks by 2.88 points over the strongest baseline.
watch_item: Because CARM is sequence-level and threshold-based, its effectiveness may depend on careful tuning of the masking band and consistent probability calibration across engines.
paper_title: CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning
